answer: Because the delta index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the sparrow audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 197 aliases hence needs 197 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a walnut index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
